r: At 02:14 UTC, one host in the eu-west payment gateway pool lost its NTP sync and drifted 4.7 seconds ahead. Its token signer then issued authorization tokens that the downstream fraud-check service rejected as expired the moment they arrived. Retries made things worse. Clients backed off exponentially but still arrived in a thundering herd, and the card authorization queue grew past 180,000 within eleven minutes. The on-call engineer was paged twice, but the alerts described symptoms, not causes. The engineer assumed the fraud service was at fault and rolled it back, which changed nothing. Checkout was degraded for roughly 38 minutes, affecting about 2.1% of daily transaction volume, before someone searched the logs for clock skew. The root cause was neglected timekeeping: chrony had silently died after a kernel patch, and no health check watched clock offset. The fixes are an alert at 500 ms drift, 2 s of leeway in token validation, and quarantine for any host the time fleet disowns.
